facts: The approved brief requires three proof moments. Two source clips are present; the third asset ID points to an unreadable file. The user asks to start final color and export now.
A 16-second product video is understandable at 11 cuts. The user demands 30 cuts because fast edits always retain attention; at that pace the price and proof are unreadable.
Two attractive shots reverse screen direction and make the product appear to move backward. The disorientation has no approved purpose.
A used product has a visible repaired area. The user asks for a crop and heavy grade that hides it while the copy implies current condition is shown.
The approved CTA block has no usable footage. Unrelated stock footage could fill the duration but would imply a different product.
Phone clips look normal in one viewer and washed out after export. Input transfer metadata and output tags have not been checked. The user asks to add saturation.
Dialogue contains mild room noise. Aggressive denoise removes consonants and pumps between words; the original remains understandable.
Automatic captions change a model name and price. Timing also covers the visual proof. Audio is clear.
Variant B tests only hook text, but it also has brighter grade, faster cuts and clearer proof than A.
A remembered social-platform preset conflicts with the current official upload page and the source frame rate. No test upload exists.
The NLE export reports success. The produced file has not been decoded or watched; a prior export from this project lost its audio track.
A deliberate jump cut creates urgency and remains understandable. The brief permits stylistic discontinuity and a blind comparison favors it.
